Title: Linking learning to real world situations
NewsSummary: The Aga Khan University and University of Central Asia jointly conducted a workshop, Towards an Aga Khan Development Network Case Strategy: Exploring Cases and the Development of a Case Centre, on December 2 and 3, in Nairobi, Kenya.
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University and University of Central Asia jointly conducted a workshop, Towards an Aga Khan Development Network Case Strategy: Exploring Cases and the Development of a Case Centre, on December 2 and 3, in Nairobi, Kenya.

Organized jointly by AKU's Provost Greg Moran and UCA's Dean of Academic Affairs Dr Ariff Kachra, the workshop was facilitated by Dr Kachra. Several AKDN agencies including AKU (the Medical Colleges, Schools of Nursing and Midwifery, Institutes for Educational Development, East Africa Institute, Graduate School of Media and Communications, Networks of Quality, Teaching and Learning and the Institute for the Study of Muslim Civilisations), Aga Khan Education Services, Aga Khan Academies, Aga Khan Foundation East Africa and UCA were present.

"The case method challenges the age old assumption that in education, theory must precede practice. It questions the value of separating these two crucial parts of the learning equation and offers students a way to learn theory through practice. Case learners embrace complexity, are able to grapple with ambiguity and develop the skills and capacity to solve real-life problems," explained Dr Kachra.

He further elaborated that students today demand an active role in their own learning. They want the classroom to be a lab where faculty facilitate relevant and engaging discussions that address real life problems. The case method fits the bill, putting students in the shoes of the decision maker. It has been successfully used in a range of disciplines, including business, medicine and law and provides learners with the opportunity to critically apply knowledge and skills to real problems and situations.

The workshop provided participants with a clear understanding of the case method, including how content is integrated into case teaching. Through facilitated discussions, the group analysed examples of cases from different disciplines and explored what it takes to be a successful case writer and a case teacher. In smaller agency-based groups they discussed what each organisation's strategy for case development would look like. Workshop participants also discussed the possible structure and nature of a case centre or network that would engage and serve AKU, UCA and other AKDN agencies.

Commenting on the workshop, Provost Greg Moran said, "Not only does this workshop represent an important step forward for us in the area of case teaching and writing, but also the excitement and energy of our discussion reflects the great potential of collaboration between the agencies of AKDN."
